title_as_printed: New Experimental Results for Simulated Sea Water Concentrates
pressure_note: Not stated as total or partial in the table. Osmotic coefficients are 'at p = p0' i.e. 'Osmotic coefficients for pressures equal to vapor pressure of pure water at each temperature' (Table 2 Note 1). Solution vapor pressure = p0 - delta p (delta p measured 'corrected to 0 C' for mercury column, per text).

composition.other_species: Simulated sea water of Na+, Mg2+, Cl-, SO4 2- only. Concentrate multiple f of the Table 11 composition (molal basis, per kg H2O; unit concentration ratio): NaCl 0.42663, Na2SO4 0.02976, MgCl2 0.06726 mol/kg H2O (ions: Na+ 0.48615, Mg2+ 0.06726, Cl- 0.56115, SO4 2- 0.02976). Molality of each salt = f x the Table 11 value. Table 11 itself is the composition used experimentally (analysed; MgCl2 about 4% above the intended Table 10 value).

extra_unmapped: concentrate multiple (column 'Concentrate Multiple of Simulated Sea Water') is the composition variable
conversion_needs: molality of NaCl, Na2SO4, MgCl2 = multiple x (0.42663, 0.02976, 0.06726) mol/kg H2O; mixture osmotic coefficient is defined by -ln a_w = 0.0180154 phi sum(m_i), sum over ionic molalities (eq. 10); a_w = (p0-dp)/p0
notes: Temperature filled down. The three concentration levels at one nominal T drift slightly because water evaporates into the vapor space; multiples are as printed.
